title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. A is a k-module carrying a coassociative (cocommutative) coalgebra structure Δ_A: A→A⊗A. F_A = Hom_k(A,-) is the functor it represents on k-modules. Because F_A commutes with ⊗ via Δ_A, the convolution product lets F_A(Γ^•X) be a ring. Grothendieck wants to describe a 'divided power structure' on the functor F_A: operations f ↦ f^{(p)} ∈ Hom(A, Γ^p X), natural in X, for f ∈ Hom(A,X).

The page proves the equivalence (2)⇔(3) of a list of conditions; (1)⇔(3) was 'déjà vu'.

Step 1 (Yoneda). A natural transformation F_A → F_A∘Γ^p is the same as an element u_p ∈ F_A(Γ^p A) = Hom(A, Γ^p A). Given u_p, the operation is f^{(p)} = Γ^p(f)∘u_p.

Step 2 (normalisations). f^{(0)} = 1 corresponds to u_0 = 1, i.e. the counit A→k=Γ^0A. f^{(1)} = f corresponds to u_1 = id_A.

Step 3 (additivity). The axiom (f+g)^{(p)} = Σ_{i+j=p} f^{(i)} g^{(j)}, with product the convolution product of the previous page, need only be checked in the universal case. Take M = A⊕A, f = inj_1, g = inj_2, so f+g = Δ: A→A⊕A (the 'diagonal' sum map, not the coproduct). Then (f+g)^{(p)} = Γ^p(Δ)∘u_p : A→Γ^p(A)→Γ^p(A⊕A) ≅ ⊕_{i+j=p} Γ^iA⊗Γ^jA. The composite Γ^p(Δ) followed by the exponential isomorphism is the p-component of the Hopf-algebra coproduct Δ_{Γ A} of the divided power algebra. The right-hand side is Σ (u_i⊗u_j)∘Δ_A.

Conclusion. The additivity axiom is equivalent to Δ_Γ∘u_p = Σ_{i+j=p} (u_i⊗u_j)∘Δ_A. In words, u = Σ u_p : A → Γ(A) is compatible with the coalgebra structures, i.e. (u_p) is a 'divided-power sequence' in the convolution sense.

Purpose. This builds a functorial, coalgebra-represented definition of PD structures, presumably for the PD de Rham complex talk (IHÉS 1976). The next page turns this into explicit questions:
- Does Hom_k(A,J) inherit PD from a PD ideal J?
- Are the u_n = u_1^{(n)} characterised by γ_{pq}∘u_{p+q} = Γ^p(u_q)∘u_p together with u_pu_q = c_{pq}u_{p+q}?
- What is the dual situation with algebras and coalgebras with divided powers?
errors: The transcription's 'u_p ∈ F_A(A) = Hom(A,Γ^p(A))' should read F_A(Γ^p A); the image shows a subscript-p-like mark on F, consistent with this.
'f^{(1)}=0' must be f^{(1)}=f, matching u_1 = id.
The notation A×A is used both for the direct sum M=A⊕A and for the tensor A⊗A in the diagram's left column. This is harmless but ambiguous.
Implicit hypothesis: A must be cocommutative (or the convolution product be commutative) for the PD axioms to make sense; this is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Natural PD-type operations Hom(A,X)→Hom(A,Γ^pX) correspond by Yoneda to elements u_p ∈ Hom(A,Γ^pA).
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda description of operations on a representable functor / polynomial laws
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (1963, 1965) for Γ as representing object of polynomial laws

ideas.what: Additivity axiom (f+g)^{(p)}=Σ f^{(i)}g^{(j)} reduced to the universal case M=A⊕A, giving Δ_Γ∘u_p = Σ(u_i⊗u_j)∘Δ_A via the exponential isomorphism Γ(A⊕A)≅ΓA⊗ΓA.
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power (Hurwitz/Hasse–Schmidt) sequences; Hopf-algebra structure of Γ(A)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby; Sweedler (divided power sequences in coalgebras); Berthelot for PD calculus

ideas.what: PD structures on convolution algebras Hom(A,B) for A a coalgebra and (B,J) a PD algebra (developed on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Divided powers on convolution algebras / duals of cocommutative coalgebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; related to Fresse's work on divided power algebras and symmetric tensors

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a 'representable' axiomatics of divided powers: PD operations on Hom(A,-) for a coalgebra A, encoded by a sequence u_p: A→Γ^pA compatible with coproducts. This leads to open questions on the next page: PD on Hom(A,J), and a characterisation of u_n=u_1^{(n)}. The reduction step is standard, but the coalgebra-indexed formulation of PD structures appears not to have been written up by him.
missed.quote: On trouve Δ(u_p) = Σ_{i+j=p} u_i ⊗ u_j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It anticipates functorial or operadic treatments of divided powers (Γ-algebras, Hom from cocommutative coalgebras into PD algebras). These have since been developed independently, so this is of mainly historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine Yoneda and universal-case reduction yielding the standard divided-power-sequence / Hopf compatibility. It is interesting only as context for the 1976 PD de Rham talk and the coalgebra-convolution viewpoint, which is now folklore.
transcription_corrections: The label on the diagonal arrow in the diagram is probably 'Δ_{Γ^p A}' or 'Δ_{Γ^•A}' (coproduct of ΓA); the vertical '≀' marks the isomorphism Γ^p(A⊕A)≅Σ Γ^iA⊗Γ^jA
Bottom of diagram: 'ou A → Γ^i(A)⊗Γ^j(A)' — the u_i⊗u_j components
Struck-out labels in 'f = inj_1, g = inj_2' are probably α, β
